userJob: Give a first screen one strong asset and one strong message without centring everything
problem: The default first screen centres a headline, a subhead and two buttons, which is the layout every competitor also reached for
worksWhen: There is one real asset worth half the screen and one sentence worth the other half
avoidWhen: The asset does not exist yet, or the message is the design, as in a manifesto or launch statement
mechanism: Asymmetric Split Hero - Text on one side, asset on the other, generous white space.
risks: Shipping it with a placeholder rectangle where the asset belongs, which reads as an unfinished template
Splitting 50/50 by reflex; the split ratio is a decision the content should make
mobileRules: Declare the collapse order below 768px: which of the two columns comes first and why
Reserve the asset's aspect ratio so the stack does not shift on load
accessibilityRules: Reading order in the DOM matches the visual order after collapse
The asset carries alt text saying what it is doing there, or is marked decorative if it truly is
genericnessNote: It is the most reached-for non-centred hero, so it escapes one default by landing in the next one unless the asset itself is specific.

userJob: Open a page where the sentence itself is the strongest material available
problem: A page with no photograph and no product gets a hero built around a stock image that says nothing about the subject
worksWhen: The subject's strongest true material is language: a position, an argument, a name, a number set large
avoidWhen: The subject is a physical thing that could be photographed, where type-only reads as a page that could not get the asset
mechanism: Editorial Manifesto Hero - Large type, no asset, almost-poster.
risks: Type at poster scale with nothing behind it becomes a dead field, which the first-screen check refuses
Reaching for it because assets are missing rather than because language is the material
mobileRules: Poster-scale type needs its own scale step at 375px; the desktop size divided by a ratio usually overflows
Keep the headline to two lines at 375px or reduce the scale, never let it clip
accessibilityRules: Large text meets 3:1 against its ground, body text 4.5:1
Set the headline as a real heading element, not a styled div
genericnessNote: Type-only heroes converge quickly on the same two or three display faces, so the face and the setting have to come from the subject.

userJob: Show several things of unequal importance in one view
problem: Unequal content gets equal cells, so importance has to be read off order rather than off the composition
worksWhen: The items genuinely differ in weight and at least two of them have real visual material
avoidWhen: All items are equal, where a grid of equal cells is honest and a bento is decoration
mechanism: Bento Grid - Asymmetric tile grouping (Apple Control Center).
risks: An empty cell left in the middle or at the end, which means the grid was planned before the content was counted
Every cell rendered as text on the same ground, which is a table wearing a grid
mobileRules: Below 768px declare the single-column order explicitly; span-based importance disappears when everything is full width
Do not preserve the desktop spans at 375px by shrinking type
accessibilityRules: Source order carries the importance the spans express visually
Each cell that is interactive is a single focusable target, not a card with three overlapping links
genericnessNote: The bento is now the default answer to any set of features, so reaching for it without counting the content is how three unrelated briefs arrive at the same page.

userJob: Shape a multi-cell grid so it does not end in a blank tile
problem: The grid is chosen first and the content is poured into it, so a five-item set lands in a six-cell grid and one tile is padding
worksWhen: Any grid whose cells have different spans, including bento, feature grids and card walls
avoidWhen: A uniform list whose count varies at runtime, where a fixed composition cannot be planned
mechanism: A bento grid has EXACTLY as many cells as you have content for. 3 items produce 3 cells (1+2 split, or 2+1, or asymmetric trio). 5 items produce 5 cells (2+3, 3+2, hero+4). If your grid has an empty cell in the middle or at the end, you planned wrong. Re-shape the grid; do not paste a blank tile.
risks: Filling the spare cell with a call to action, which puts a commitment in a scanning region
Padding the set with a weak sixth item so the grid closes
mobileRules: The single-column order is declared per item, not inherited from the grid's visual reading order
accessibilityRules: A blank tile with no content and no label is announced as an empty region; remove it rather than hiding it from assistive technology
genericnessNote: Counting content before choosing a composition produces a different grid per brief.

userJob: Lay out items whose natural heights differ, without cropping them all to one ratio
problem: A gallery of mixed-ratio images is forced into a uniform grid, so portraits get cropped to landscapes and the set loses the thing that made it a set
worksWhen: Item height carries real information: image ratio, quote length, drawing extent
avoidWhen: Items are comparable and the reader needs to compare them, where ragged rows make comparison harder
mechanism: Masonry Layout - Staggered grid, no fixed row height.
risks: Column-ordered masonry breaks reading order, so a chronological set reads down each column rather than across
Late-loading images reflow the whole column set unless each item declares its ratio
mobileRules: One column at 375px turns masonry into a list; check that the list order is still the order you intended
Declare width and height or aspect-ratio on every item to avoid cumulative layout shift
accessibilityRules: Ensure DOM order matches the intended reading order, since visual column flow and source order can diverge
Interactive items keep a visible focus indicator that is not clipped by the column gap
genericnessNote: Masonry reads as a portfolio device by default, so on a non-portfolio brief it has to earn its place from the content's real ratios.

userJob: Carry a reader through an ordered argument where each step replaces the last
problem: An ordered argument is laid out as consecutive blocks, so the reader sees the steps but not the replacement, and the order reads as arbitrary
worksWhen: The content is genuinely sequential and each step supersedes the previous one
avoidWhen: The reader needs to compare steps side by side, or the page's job is to be scanned
mechanism: Sticky-Stack Sections - Sections that pin and stack on scroll.
risks: Pinning a section taller than the viewport, which traps the reader in a region they cannot scroll past on a short screen
Using it for content that is not ordered, which claims a sequence that does not exist
mobileRules: At 375px a pinned section needs its own height budget; the desktop pin distance usually exceeds the mobile viewport
Provide a non-pinned fallback below a stated width rather than shrinking the pinned composition
accessibilityRules: Under prefers-reduced-motion the sections render as an ordinary stacked sequence with the same content and order
Keyboard scrolling reaches every pinned step; a pin that only responds to wheel events strands keyboard users
genericnessNote: Scroll pinning is the signature move of the current agency default, so it needs a reason from the subject rather than from the effect.

userJob: Show two related tracks moving against each other as the reader scrolls
problem: Two parallel narratives, such as a process and its output, are stacked in sequence so the relationship between them is stated rather than shown
worksWhen: The two tracks are genuinely paired and the pairing is the point
avoidWhen: One track is decorative, in which case the effect is carrying an empty half
mechanism: Split-Screen Scroll - Two halves sliding in opposite directions.
risks: Opposing motion causes disorientation at speed; the effect needs a rate limit
The pairing breaks at any width where the halves cannot both be read
mobileRules: Below 768px the two halves become a sequence, and the pairing has to be restated in words or by adjacency
Opposed scroll on a touch device competes with the browser's own scroll physics
accessibilityRules: prefers-reduced-motion renders both tracks as static, paired blocks
Neither half may become unreachable by keyboard when the other is in motion
genericnessNote: Opposed scroll is a library demo before it is a design, so the pairing has to come from the subject's own two tracks.

userJob: Give a long ordered page a readable sense of position
problem: A long page offers no sense of where the reader is in the argument, so they either stop early or scroll past the part they came for
worksWhen: The page really is a path: a route, a process, a timeline, a run of stages with an end
avoidWhen: The page is a set rather than a sequence, where a path claims an order that does not exist
mechanism: Scroll Progress Path - SVG line drawing along scroll.
risks: The path draws something that is not actually a path, which is a structural claim with nothing behind it
A decorative line at the page edge reads as chrome and gets ignored
mobileRules: At 375px a marginal path competes with the content column; either move it inline or drop it
Path length recalculates on resize, so cache the geometry or it jumps on orientation change
accessibilityRules: The path is decorative unless it also carries position in text; if it is the only position indicator, expose the position as text too
Under prefers-reduced-motion the path renders complete rather than animating
genericnessNote: Line-drawing on scroll is common enough that it only reads as designed when the line traces something the subject actually has.

userJob: Let a headline carry a moving image without laying type over video
problem: Type set over video is unreadable at some frames and needs a scrim, which flattens the image the video was there for
worksWhen: There is real footage of the real subject and the headline is short enough to work as a window
avoidWhen: The footage is stock, or the headline is longer than about three words, where the mask becomes noise
mechanism: Text Mask Reveal - Massive type as transparent window to video.
risks: Contrast cannot be guaranteed frame by frame, so the headline can become illegible without warning
Fallback for browsers or modes without the mask often loses the headline entirely
mobileRules: At 375px the mask window is too small to read the footage through; consider a static frame instead
Video autoplay on cellular is a cost the visitor did not agree to; provide a poster frame
accessibilityRules: The headline exists as real text in the DOM, with the mask as presentation only
Under prefers-reduced-motion the video is replaced by a still frame and the headline stays readable
genericnessNote: It is a recognisable showreel device, so on a non-showreel brief it announces the effect rather than the subject.

userJob: Give a dense set of cards a hover state that does not repaint the whole card
problem: Card hover states default to lift and shadow, which animates layout-adjacent properties and reads the same on every site
worksWhen: There are many cards on a dark or mid ground, and the pointer is the primary input
avoidWhen: Touch is the primary input, where the state never fires and the design has no hover layer at all
mechanism: Spotlight Border Card - Borders illuminate under cursor.
risks: It is pointer-only, so on touch the card has no state and reads as flat
Tracking pointer position per card is a per-frame cost that scales with the card count
mobileRules: Define the touch state separately: the spotlight is not a fallback for a press state
Never let hover be the only way to discover that a card is interactive
accessibilityRules: The keyboard focus state is at least as visible as the hover state, and meets 3:1 on its own
prefers-reduced-motion drops the tracking and leaves a static border change
genericnessNote: It arrived as a component library demo and spread from there, so it now signals the library rather than the brand.

userJob: Open a dialog without losing the user's sense of where it came from
problem: A modal appears centred with no spatial relationship to the control that opened it, so the user loses their place in a dense screen
worksWhen: The trigger is a visible object on a busy screen and the dialog is about that object
avoidWhen: The dialog is a global action with no originating object, where morphing from an arbitrary control invents a relationship
mechanism: Morphing Modal - Button expands into its own dialog.
risks: The morph delays the moment the dialog becomes usable, which is motion sitting between an intent and its result
Return focus is easy to lose when the trigger is removed or scrolled out during the transition
mobileRules: At 375px the morph target is usually the full screen, so the transition reduces to a slide; declare that explicitly
Ensure the dismiss control is inside the thumb's reach, not only at the top corner
accessibilityRules: Focus moves into the dialog on open and returns to the trigger on close
The dialog traps focus while open and is dismissible by Escape
Under prefers-reduced-motion the dialog appears without the morph
genericnessNote: The morph is a means, not a look, but the default styling that ships with it is what makes it recognisable.

userJob: Choose a first-screen composition that is not the centred stack by reflex
problem: Centred headline, centred subhead, two centred buttons is the composition that appears when no composition was chosen
worksWhen: A non-centred structure is available: split screen, left content against a right asset, asymmetric negative space, a pinned structure
avoidWhen: The brief is editorial, a manifesto or a launch announcement, where the message itself is the design and centring is the argument
mechanism: Treat the centred hero as the autopilot answer and write it down before building anything else, then build one of the alternatives unless you can argue the centred version from the subject. Name which structure you chose and what it gets that the others do not.
risks: Swapping one default for another: the left-text right-image split is the second most available answer
Choosing asymmetry as a style rather than because the content has unequal weight
mobileRules: Every non-centred desktop structure collapses to a single column at 375px, so state which element leads and why
A composition that only works at 1440px is not a composition, it is a screenshot
accessibilityRules: Centred or not, the first screen carries one h1 and a visible focus path into the primary control
genericnessNote: Naming the autopilot composition before building is the mechanism that makes this post reduce sameness rather than replace one default with another.

userJob: Stop a long page from repeating one layout family down its whole length
problem: Once a section shape works, it gets reused for every following section, so eight sections read as one section eight times
worksWhen: Any page with more than four content sections
avoidWhen: A deliberately repetitive structure, such as an index or a catalogue, where repetition is the information
mechanism: Once a layout family is used for a section, that family appears at most once more on the page. A landing page with eight sections uses at least four different families. Alternating image-left and image-right counts as one family, and three consecutive image plus text splits is a failure rather than variety.
risks: Counting variety by content rather than by shape, so four different topics in one shape read as one page
Breaking the pattern with a decorative full-width band that carries nothing
mobileRules: At 375px most families collapse to a single column, so the variety has to survive in spacing, rhythm and type rather than in columns
accessibilityRules: Each section is a real landmark or heading so a screen reader user can tell the sections apart even when the shapes collapse
genericnessNote: Counting layout families is a mechanical check that produces different pages for different content sets.

userJob: Decide what actually occupies the first screen before writing any of it
problem: The first screen defaults to a heading, a subhead and a button on a flat ground, which is words on paint and has not started the argument
worksWhen: Every build, on every surface, because the first screen is the whole argument in one frame
avoidWhen: Never on a page that is meant to be seen; it applies even when the page is a form
mechanism: Name the object that owns the first viewport before building it: a drawn form, a photograph, a diagram, a piece of type set large enough to be an image, a field of texture with one thing on it. Then check three things. Painted matter occupies a real share of the screen. There is no large rectangle of untouched ground. One element is unmistakably this subject and could not be cropped into a competitor's site unnoticed.
risks: Calling a gradient background painted matter, which is paint rather than matter
Meeting the share requirement with a stock image that belongs to no subject
mobileRules: The object has to own the 375px viewport too, which usually means a different crop rather than the same crop scaled
Reserve the object's aspect ratio so the first paint does not jump
accessibilityRules: If the object is an image it carries alt text saying what it is doing there
If the object is type, it is real text at a size that still meets contrast against its ground
genericnessNote: Naming the object forces a choice the category cannot make, which is why the check is about presence rather than about style.

userJob: Stop the page's one good idea from being the only designed thing on it
problem: The strongest move is spent on the signature in the first screen and everything below is chrome, so cutting one drawing makes the page generic
worksWhen: The page has a signature device and more than one measurement or fact worth rendering
avoidWhen: A single-screen page with one fact, where a second reading would repeat the first
mechanism: Render one of the subject's own measurements as something readable in a second, at least twice, and put the second one outside the first screen. The second must read from a different fact than the signature does, because the cheapest answer to doing it again is the same drawing twice. Record both in the direction record with the fact each renders and the selector.
risks: Repeating the same visual device with different numbers, which is one idea used twice
Inventing a measurement to have something to draw, which is a claim without a source
mobileRules: Both readings survive at 375px or are replaced by a version that reads at that width, not merely scaled down
accessibilityRules: Each rendered measurement carries its value as text next to or inside the drawing, so it is not colour or width alone
A drawn gauge is labelled with its unit and its worst case, not only its current value
genericnessNote: Two different facts rendered in two different forms cannot be reused on the next brief, which is the point.

userJob: Let a buyer price a made-to-measure or configured product from measurements and options they already hold, before contacting anyone
problem: A made-to-order trade hides price behind call for a quote, so the buyer rings, describes the job badly, and is told a number they cannot check against anything
worksWhen: The price is a function of inputs the buyer can supply without expertise: dimensions, a material choice, a quantity, a delivery choice
avoidWhen: The price genuinely needs a survey, a site visit or a drawing, in which case the page states what the visit decides rather than faking a total
mechanism: Put the configurator where the object is, not on a separate quote page, and carry the running total from the first input rather than revealing it at the end. Compute in the browser so the figure answers inside a tenth of a second and needs no network. Every input names the trade's own unit and says how to take it. The total states its own arithmetic, area or quantity and rate, so the buyer can check it against the price list on the same page. The result is a written specification the seller can work from, and it says plainly what is and is not being charged at that moment.
risks: A total that animates or recalculates visibly reads as a slot machine near money
Rounding that is not stated, so the buyer's arithmetic and the page's disagree by a krone
Hiding the rate so the total cannot be checked, which converts a calculator into a quote
mobileRules: Numeric inputs use inputmode numeric so the phone keypad appears
The running total stays visible while the fields are filled, docked or repeated, never only above the fold
Field labels and their units sit on one line at 375 or the unit moves into the field's own hint
accessibilityRules: The total is announced with role=status when it changes, so it is not a silent visual update
Every validation message sits on the field that caused it and is referenced by aria-describedby
The whole configurator completes on the keyboard alone with a visible indicator at each stop
genericnessNote: The mechanism is a shape, not a look; it becomes generic only if the configurator is styled as a SaaS pricing card rather than as the trade's own order paper

userJob: Close a sale on a page that has no payment provider and should not pretend to have one
problem: A page with no checkout still ships a button that looks like one, so the buyer expects a confirmation and receives an email form, or worse, believes an order was placed
worksWhen: The trade takes orders by telephone, invoice or collection, and the site's job is to produce something unambiguous for both sides to work from
avoidWhen: A real checkout exists, where a written specification is an extra step between the buyer and the thing they came to buy
mechanism: The commit control produces a specification rather than a transaction: every input the buyer gave, the computed figures, the lead time and the handover, in one block they can read back over a telephone or send as it stands. The control's word says what it does, and the same word appears in the result. Nothing on the page implies a charge has been made, and the specification states in its own words when payment happens.
risks: A control labelled Order or Buy on a page that cannot take money
A success state that looks like a receipt
Losing the buyer's inputs when the specification appears, so a correction means starting again
mobileRules: The specification is selectable and copyable at 375 without horizontal scrolling
The control does not sit under a sticky element at the bottom of a phone screen
accessibilityRules: Focus moves to the specification when it appears, or it is announced with role=status
The specification is real text, never an image or a canvas rendering
genericnessNote: It is an honesty constraint on the commit control, and honesty about a shop's real process is the opposite of a template

userJob: Sell something the seller has a fixed and unrepeatable quantity of
problem: Scarcity is either invented as pressure or hidden entirely, and a buyer who orders past the real limit finds out after they have committed
worksWhen: The brief gives a real remaining quantity with no reorder date: one batch, one salvaged lot, one sheet
avoidWhen: Stock is replenished on a schedule, where a remaining count is noise that changes daily and teaches the buyer to ignore it
mechanism: State the remaining quantity in the unit the buyer is ordering in, beside the option it limits rather than in a banner. When an order would exceed it, the refusal names the number that is left and appears on the field that caused it, before the commit control is reachable. Say what happens when it runs out in the seller's own words, including when the honest answer is that there is no more.
risks: A countdown or a colour that implies urgency the brief never gave
Showing a remaining count for something that is restocked, which reads as theatre once a buyer sees it change
mobileRules: The remaining quantity sits with its option, not in a separate panel the phone pushes below the fold
accessibilityRules: The limit is text, not colour alone
The refusal is announced and focus moves to the field it belongs to
genericnessNote: The number comes from the brief and belongs to one seller, so it cannot be reused across projects
